title: Down Beat cover and Time profile
summary: Johnston reads other press coverage of him.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: And I think this is certainly a compliment to you because here's another Down Beat from May 5th 1948 and there is a very, very handsome and slender (LAUGHTER) ....
Jimmy McPartland on the cover. (LAUGHTER). And there is also Time Magazine which, let me see, I don't know what date it is.

When I had just got back from Europe, the War rather and we were playing at a place called 'The Brass Rail' in Chicago on Randolph and Dedborn. And a guy came in and did this write up. Jim Bell, James Bell did the write up.
Well he says, at that point that you were forty but looked thirty. And I would have to
say now you're 66 and you look 46. (LAUGHTER). Thank you dear. Thank you Helen.

And he says, on a stage stuck up behind the bar, Jimmy drove out "Jazz Me Blues" and "Nobody's Sweetheart" in the same hard terse middle range faces that Chicago jazz fans had first heard in the twenties. And he says, twenty five years ago Jimmy McPartland was a thin, we keep coming back to that don't we? (LAUGHTER). Good looking kid who had been playing the cornet ever since he could remember. And he and the gang at Austin High spent their time practicing in vacant houses. Played for PTA sponsored dances and listening to an old juke box with a 'Straw and Spoon' which you mentioned earlier.
With a cook joint across the street from Austin High. When they weren't practicing themselves they were listening to big timers. And of course, we went through those names, King Oliver and...
